startingState: Working copy was byte-identical to upstream (diff clean) — no interrupted edits to repair; localized from scratch.

font.reason: The card's only text is tiny, low-emphasis technical chrome (a caption strip in muted #5b6480). Vazirmatn is the neutral product-UI Persian voice, variable weight, and has full coverage of Persian digits, punctuation and ZWNJ. Loaded via FaRoot (family='Vazirmatn') — verified rendering in the stills (no fallback look). The original's SF Mono / monospace has no Persian-joining-safe counterpart in the kit (Vazir Code renders Persian stretched/unjoined per lessons), so the Persian caption uses Vazirmatn.

textChanges.persian: ورود: تأخیر پلکانی + گرادیان در مقادیر
textChanges.why: The original caption is an anime.js API call string. The card's own source prompt says these captions are technique annotations, not content, and in a real film must become a semantic title or be removed. Keeping raw English code on screen would also violate the 'no unintended foreign text' rule. The Persian caption states what beat 1 does: staggered entry delay with a value gradient (height/hue/travel/blur).

textChanges.persian: نبض: پلکانی از مرکز، بیشینهٔ دامنه در میانه
textChanges.why: Same reasoning; the Persian caption states what beat 2 does: pulse staggered from the center with maximum amplitude in the middle. Persian typography checked: Persian ی/ک, no Arabic ي/ك, natural tech-demo wording (not word-for-word), no orphan letters.

timingBeats: All beats preserved exactly: caption fade-in seg(t,0.04,0.12), HARD CUT between captions at t=0.52 (f78), entry cascade d=i*0.02 with window 0.22 outCubic, center pulse 0.56+distC*0.13, endpoints settle by t=0.87 with the design's intentional static hold to t=1. No string-length-driven beat shifts exist (captions are not typed/staggered). VALUE_STAGGER_GRADIENT_DURATION=150, fps 30, 1920x1080, N=16, seeds, easings: all unchanged.

rtlDecisions.what: Beat-1 stagger/cascade origin and the hue/height/travel/blur ramp (bars + decorative dots)
rtlDecisions.action: MIRRORED: bars and dots anchored with right: (8+i*5.4)% (+1.2% inward offset for dots) instead of left:. Bar i=0 (hue 200 blue, tallest, first to move, longest travel/blur) now sits at the RIGHT edge; the ramp reads right-to-left.
rtlDecisions.why: The stagger origin is the 'first' element — reading-order semantics (checklist: first item = right-most for RTL). The gradient ramp and cascade order carry layout-direction meaning, so they flip; magnitude/direction of every animated value (translateY, scaleY, blur, brightness) is unchanged.

rtlDecisions.what: Beat-2 center pulse (from center, distC=|i-7.5|/7.5, distC*0.13 delay, amp=lerp(1-distC,0.06,0.42), brightness 1+pulse*0.55)
rtlDecisions.why: Physically symmetric about the center axis; a center origin has no reading direction. Verified visually at f97: identical bulge/brightness shape in fa and orig.

rtlDecisions.action: KEPT centered (left:50% + translateX(-50%) is direction-neutral); direction:rtl + unicodeBidi:plaintext from kit/faText; letterSpacing forced to 0 (the original 1.5px tracking on Latin mono must not survive on joined Persian); fontSize fs(10) x1.1 per kit; color #5b6480 and top:9% unchanged.
rtlDecisions.why: Centered chrome text; Persian joins break under letter-spacing; Persian x-height compensates via fs().

rtlDecisions.what: Bar visual physics (vertical entrance, 180deg gradient, borderRadius 5, glow shadow, dots row)
rtlDecisions.why: Vertical motion (gravity axis) and symmetric glow/radii carry no reading direction.

rasterHandling: No raster/video assets in this demo — everything is pure DOM divs; nothing to sanitize or mirror.

leftoverScan: Grep of the card dir: no letterSpacing, no textTransform/uppercase, no left/translateX/marginLeft/paddingLeft/clipPath/inset/gradient-angle/transformOrigin hits beyond the mirrored right-anchors, the centered caption (left:50% + translateX(-50%), direction-neutral) and transformOrigin '50% 100%' (vertical, physical). Zero Chinese/English on-screen text in the Persian render.
concerns: The original caption strings were anime.js API code; they were replaced with semantic Persian captions as the card's source prompt itself prescribes. A reviewer wanting the literal code kept could disagree, but keeping English code would violate the no-foreign-text rule and the prompt explicitly sanctions semantic titles.
Chinese comments from upstream remain in code comments (staggerVal/BARS blocks) — code comments are not on-screen text; upstream reference values were kept for fidelity auditing.
